spec.name: kb-trip-xor-rol-add
spec.limitations: Byte-local only, so equal plaintext bytes at different offsets produce equal ciphertext bytes (no cross-byte diffusion). Because every step is public except the three XOR_K steps, a single known plaintext/ciphertext pair lets an observer invert the public steps and solve K directly; known-plaintext confidentiality therefore fails outright. Provides no integrity or authentication. Rotation amounts and constants (2, 5, 57, 212) are arbitrary and unanalyzed.
spec.math: Per byte: x1=b xor K; x2=ROL2(x1); x3=(x2+57) mod 256; x4=x3 xor K; x5=ROL5(x4); x6=(x5+212) mod 256; y=x6 xor K. Every step is a bijection on the 256 byte values (xor with a constant is an involution, add mod 256 is a cyclic shift, ROLn is a bit permutation), so the composition is a bijection and its inverse is the reverse-order composition of the inverses.
spec.assumptions: The engine substitutes the same secret byte K at all three *_key positions and ignores the placeholder 0; bytes are 8-bit, arithmetic is mod 256, ROL is a left rotation inside the byte; K is uniform and independent per challenge.
